title: RL4Sys: A Lightweight System-driven RL Framework for Drop-in Integration in System Optimization
problem: Reinforcement learning shows promise for system optimization but existing frameworks (RLlib, Ray) introduce substantial integration overhead when embedded in system software, limiting practical deployment.
motivation: Systems researchers want to leverage RL for online system optimization (caching, scheduling, routing), but current frameworks require significant integration effort and add unacceptable runtime overhead.
method: RL4Sys embeds a lightweight client in the target system that watches behavior and runs a cached machine-learning policy, keeping overhead below 6%. Separately, remote trainers asynchronously improve the policy from the recorded observations—communicating through zero-copy gRPC (sending data without duplicating it) with adaptive batching that groups updates for efficiency. This split between a minimal local client and powerful remote trainers avoids the heavy integration overhead of traditional RL frameworks.
key_novelty: The innovation is achieving practical system-level reinforcement learning with under 6% overhead by pairing a lightweight embedded client with remote asynchronous trainers using zero-copy communication.
contributions: RL4Sys lightweight RL framework for systems
Minimal client (<6% overhead) for seamless integration
Zero-copy gRPC + adaptive batching for efficiency
220% higher throughput vs. RLlib in environment-oriented settings
limitations: Abstract-only; specific optimization use cases not detailed; convergence comparison limited; hardware requirements not specified
primary_theme: Lightweight RL Framework for System-Level Optimization
